# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format is based on
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), starting at `v0.0.1`.

## [Unreleased]

- **The sourced-weight WARRANT gate — audited, verified FORMAL BLOCKER (no invention).** The generic
  self-adjoint multiplier `multiplier_selfAdjoint w` is proved for an *arbitrary* real weight; the
  reviewer's next gate is a *sourced* unbounded weight — a typed parent/child UOR refinement relation
  whose DERIVED real evaluator `w : Nat → Real` (a) is zero/RH-free, (b) restricts on its first 24 levels
  to `atlasSeedWeight : Fin 24 → Real`, and (c) grows cofinally. An exhaustive read-only audit of every
  Atlas/UOR/Cohomology/E8 source in the repo **and** of the external registered dependency
  (`UOR-Framework v0.5.2`, vendored at `.lake/packages/uor/`) finds **no such source exists**, and records
  the precise reasons rather than inventing one:
  * The only tower-shaped *sourced* object degenerates: `AtlasAddressing.atlasModulus_degenerate`
    (`atlasModulus (k+5) = 0`), `atlasPrime_finite`. The `Fin 24` spectral seed is a SEPARATE fact —
    `atlasEig = blockEig` over `(T,O)=(3,8)`, provably unconnected to the addressing tower (no theorem
    ties them into one seed-refining operator tower).
  * The seed is bounded (`atlasSeedEig_bounded`, values in `[−1,10]`) and finite-rank `M₂₄ ⊕ 0`
    (`atlasObs_vanishes_off_carrier`, `atlasObsEig_seam`) — not cofinal.
  * Every unbounded real weight in the repo is a SELF-DECLARED invention (`atlasShiftDiag`,
    `blockLadderEval`) — fails the "derived from the relation" clause; both stay frozen.
  * The external registered source (`UOR-Framework v0.5.2`, a resolved git dependency pinned in
    `lake-manifest.json`) carries an infinite typed level object `WittLevel` (wraps every `Nat`; its
    named constants coincide with the Atlas fixture numbers 24/96/128/12288) and lift-chain/tower
    CERTIFICATE machinery, but NO real-valued evaluator (only per-individual `Float` annotations, and the
    `WittLevel` readout is the `Nat` level index, not a real diagonal). The F1 root DOES import six UOR
    ontology modules (`UOR.Structures` + `UOR.Individuals.{Op,Schema,Convergence,Division,Homology}`), but
    none defines a `Nat → Real` evaluator, and F1 imports none of the Witt-level/lift-chain machinery
    (`UOR.Enums`/`Pipeline`/`Enforcement`); `atlasEig = blockEig` over `(T,O)=(3,8)`, independent of any
    imported UOR evaluator.
  The verified boundary is recorded in `FinAtlasOperator.lean`'s "WHY NO UNBOUNDED SOURCED LIFT /
  EXTERNAL REGISTERED UOR SOURCE, AUDITED" docstring. **The missing typed refinement source is the formal
  blocker** (an audit conclusion in prose, not a mechanized Lean theorem); no weight is instantiated,
  `BlockLadder`/`atlasShiftDiag` stay frozen, HP-crux delta stays ZERO.

- **The real-weight diagonal multiplier is a genuine SELF-ADJOINT operator — generic gate complete**
  (`Square/DlimMultiplier*.lean`, culminating in `Square/DlimMultiplierAdjoint.lean`). For an ARBITRARY
  real weight `w : Nat → Real`, the diagonal multiplier `M_w` on the completed pre-Hilbert space is
  built as a choice-free RELATION (its graph `MulGraph`, domain `MulDom`) and shown to be a genuine
  self-adjoint operator — not symmetry, not a coordinatewise statement, not a nominal predicate:
  * `AdjGraph` — the adjoint by the inner-product UNIVERSAL PROPERTY: `(Y,Z) ∈ Γ(M_w*)` iff
    `⟨M_w X, Y⟩ = ⟨X, Z⟩` for every domain pair `(X, M_w X)`. `AdjGraph_congr_adj` (setoid descent),
    `adj_unique_adj` (adjoint-output uniqueness via basis testing + coordinate separation).
  * `adj_of_dom_adj` — the easy inclusion `D(M_w) ⊆ D(M_w*)` from the symmetry `mult_symm_sy`;
    `dom_of_adj_adj` — the HARD MAXIMALITY `D(M_w*) ⊆ D(M_w)` (what upgrades symmetric to
    self-adjoint), proved by testing the adjoint relation against the dense coordinate basis `of e_i`
    and separating coordinates; `dom_eq_adj` — `Dom(M_w*) = Dom(M_w)`.
  * `selfadjoint_adj` — graph-level self-adjointness `Γ(M_w*) = Γ(M_w)`; `MultiplierSelfAdjoint` /
    `multiplier_selfAdjoint` — the packaged predicate bundling DENSITY (`MulDom_dense_mp`), sequential
    CLOSEDNESS (`MulGraph_closed_cl`), graph self-adjointness, and domain equality.
  Enabling analysis, ζ-free, cleared along the way: the SHARP (uncancelled) Cauchy–Schwarz via
  apartness (`completedInner_re_cs_sharp`) and the genuine, unconditional, full-complex fixed-vector
  LIMIT continuity (`inner_fixed_tendsto_scs`), plus Parseval (`completedInner_parseval_sy`).
  **HONEST SCOPE — "self-adjoint," NOT "unbounded."** The theorem holds for EVERY real weight,
  including `w ≡ 0` and every bounded weight; it proves densely-defined + closed + self-adjoint, hence
  only *possibly* unbounded. Actual unboundedness is a SEPARATE claim needing a growth hypothesis on `w`
  and its transfer to the operator norm — not established here (the `628f21f` commit message overstated
  it as "unbounded"; the accurate reading is "densely-defined, closed, possibly-unbounded self-adjoint
  multiplier"). **HP-crux delta is ZERO**: this is a GENERIC theorem over an arbitrary `w`; no Atlas
  weight is instantiated. Instantiating a *sourced* unbounded weight is the open warrant gate, and the
  Atlas refinement tower is already proven to degenerate past the `Fin 24` seed
  (`AtlasAddressing.atlasModulus_degenerate`, `atlasPrime_finite`; `FinAtlasOperator` "no unbounded
  sourced lift"), so no such weight is available without a genuinely new source. `BlockLadder` and
  `atlasShiftDiag` remain frozen. Strictly ζ-free, sqrt-free, division-free, choice-free
  `[propext, Quot.sound]`; audit coverage 5546, no-smuggling PASS.

- **The real-scale Mellin dilation covariance with the rational covariance DERIVED** (new
  `Square/MellinHatDilateCovarianceRealDerived.lean`): the real-scale covariance
  `cⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR c φ) = mellinHat φ` (`mellinHat_dilate_covariance_real_derived`), with the
  "covariance holds at each rational approximant" hypothesis (`hcov` of the base capstone) now DERIVED
  rather than assumed. It is discharged from the more primitive, checkable decay data — the
  per-approximant bounds `hdec_qk`/`hdec_fine_qk` and the schedule regularity `hReg_qk` — through the
  unconditional `covariance_at_rational_dilateTestR` (its scalar `ofQ (qpow q (n+1))` bridged to the
  capstone's `Rpow (ofQ q) (n+1)` by `Rpow_ofQ`). So the covariance is no longer assumed on the rationals;
  it is established there from the tiling-based unconditional covariance, and only `hbound` (the
  fast-approximation continuity rate) remains an explicit input. **Honest scope**: object-grounding
  substrate; `hbound` and the diagonal `q_k = c.seq(fast(k))` construction are the deferred plumbing. It
  builds NO factorization theorem, NO grounding of `v = ĝ`, and NO step-4 band-coupling positivity
  (`ArchDominatesPrime`), which is RH. The crux fields stay `none`.

- **The real-scale Mellin dilation covariance** (new `Square/MellinHatDilateCovarianceReal.lean`): the
  unconditional rational-scale covariance `qⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilate_q φ) = mellinHat φ` passed to a REAL
  scale `c` — the rung-6 goal of the transform bridge:

      `cⁿ⁺¹ · mellinHat (dilateTestR c φ) n = mellinHat φ n`

  (`mellinHat_dilate_covariance_real`). The rational-scale covariance holds at every rational `q`
  (`covariance_at_rational_dilateTestR`) and the combination `F(c) = cⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR c φ)` is
  scale-continuous (`covComb_scale_split`); so `F` is a continuous function constant (`= mellinHat φ`) on
  the rationals, and by rational density + the Archimedean squeeze (`Req_of_real_null_family`) it is
  constant on all of `ℝ`. This is the passage the roadmap named — *the rational covariance can pass to
  real scales* — now made. The two hypotheses `hcov` (rational-scale covariance at the approximants) and
  `hbound` (the continuity gap is a null family — the approximants converge fast enough) are the honest,
  dischargeable analytic inputs; **neither is RH-equivalent**. **Honest scope**: object-grounding
  substrate for the convolution/Mellin factorization (evaluating the inner `x`-integral at a real scale,
  toward grounding `v = ĝ`). It builds NO factorization theorem `M[f⋆g]=M[f]·M[g]` on its own, NO
  grounding of `v = ĝ`, and — emphatically — NO step-4 band-coupling positivity (`ArchDominatesPrime`),
  which is RH. The crux fields stay `none`.

- **The Archimedean squeeze for Bishop reals** (new `Analysis/RealNullFamily.lean`): if two reals are
  within `C/(k+1)` of each other for EVERY `k`, they are equal —

      `(∀ k, |x − y| ≤ C/(k+1)) ⟹ x ≈ y`

  (`Req_of_real_null_family`). Fixing a sequence index `n`, the `k`-family gives
  `|(x−y).seq n| ≤ C/(k+1) + 2/(n+1)` for all `k`, so `Qarch_gen` kills the `C/(k+1)` term to leave
  `≤ 2/(n+1)`, and `Req_of_lin_bound` turns that into `x − y ≈ 0`. **Why (rung 6)**: this is the
  real-scale covariance capstone's final step — the combination `F(c) = cⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR c φ)`
  is continuous (`covComb_scale_split`) and constant on the rationals (`covariance_at_rational_dilateTestR`),
  so approximating `c` by rationals `q_k → c` gives `|F(c) − mellinHat φ| ≤ C/(k+1)` for every `k`, and this
  lemma concludes `F(c) = mellinHat φ`. **Honest scope**: a general Bishop-real equality-from-null-family
  lemma only — NO covariance, NO factorization, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4
  (band-coupling positivity) is RH; crux `none`.

- **The covariance combination is scale-continuous** (new `Square/CovCombScaleCont.lean`): the object
  `F(c) = cⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR c φ) n` — whose value the real-scale dilation covariance asserts is the
  constant `mellinHat φ n` — varies continuously in the real dilation scale `c`. For every depth `j`,

      `|F(c) − F(c')| ≤ Sⁿ⁺¹·((φ.L + head_j)·|c−c'| + 4/(j+1)) + Bφ·((n+1)·Sⁿ·|c−c'|)`,

  `head_j = Σ_{m<N_j} φ.L·(m+2)·(powWinTest m n).M`, `N_j = digammaMidx(C·2ⁿ) j`, `Bφ` the finite Mellin
  magnitude bound (`covComb_scale_split`). As `j → ∞`, `c' → c` the RHS → 0. The mixed-product identity
  splits `F(c) − F(c')` into `cⁿ⁺¹·(M_c − M_c') + (cⁿ⁺¹ − c'ⁿ⁺¹)·M_c'`; the first is bounded by
  `|cⁿ⁺¹| ≤ Sⁿ⁺¹` times the Mellin scale-continuity `mellinHat_scale_split`, the second by the polynomial
  base-Lipschitz `Rpow_base_lip` times the Mellin magnitude bound `mellinHat_abs_le`. **Why (rung 6)**:
  this is the last continuity step before the real-scale covariance — `F` continuous plus `F` constant on
  the rationals (`covariance_at_rational_dilateTestR`) plus rational density forces `F(c) = mellinHat φ n`
  at every real `c`. **Honest scope**: the split-at-depth scale-continuity of `F` only — NO real-scale
  covariance (that is the capstone), NO factorization, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4
  (band-coupling positivity) is RH; crux `none`.

- **The Mellin transform has a bounded magnitude, uniformly in the dilation scale** (new
  `Square/MellinHatBound.lean`): a finite, scale-INDEPENDENT bound

      `|mellinHat (dilateTestR c φ) n| ≤ φ.M/(n+1) + (Σ_{m<N₀} φ.M·(powWinTest m n).M) + 2`,

  `N₀ = digammaMidx (C·2ⁿ) 0` (`mellinHat_abs_le`). The bound depends only on `φ.M, C, n` — not on the
  real scale `c`, since `dilateTestR c φ` has `.M = φ.M`. The proof is deliberately CRUDE — no decay, no
  telescoping: the compact moment is `mellinMoment_abs_le`, and the tail `twTail` (an `Rlim` of partial
  sums) obeys `|twTail| ≤ |0th partial sum| + 2` by the uniform Bishop-limit rate (`Rabs_dist_Rlim` at
  `j = 0`), with the finite `N₀`-term 0th sum bounded term-by-term by `|twTerm m| ≤ φ.M·(powWinTest m n).M`
  (`twTerm_crude_bound`, via `riemannIntegralI_abs_le_window`). The per-window constant growing with `m` is
  harmless — only finitely many terms are summed; the infinite tail is absorbed by the `2/(j+1)` limit
  rate. **Why (rung 6)**: the covariance capstone shows `F(c) = cⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR c φ)` continuous
  by `|F(c) − F(c')| ≤ |cⁿ⁺¹ − c'ⁿ⁺¹|·|M_c| + |c'ⁿ⁺¹|·|M_c − M_c'|`; the first term needs this finite
  `|M_c|` bound. **Honest scope**: a finite magnitude bound on the Mellin transform only — NO covariance,
  NO F-continuity, NO factorization, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4 (band-coupling
  positivity) is RH; crux `none`.

- **The rational-scale dilation covariance in `dilateTestR` form** (new `Square/CovarianceAtRational.lean`):
  the unconditional rational-scale Mellin dilation covariance `qⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTest q φ) = mellinHat φ`
  read against the real-scale dilation:

      `qⁿ⁺¹ · mellinHat (dilateTestR (ofQ q) φ) n = mellinHat φ n`

  (`covariance_at_rational_dilateTestR`). A one-step composition: pull the representation bridge
  `mellinHat_bridge` (which equates `mellinHat (dilateTest q φ)` and `mellinHat (dilateTestR (ofQ q) φ)`)
  inside the scalar `qⁿ⁺¹` (`Rmul_congr`), then apply `mellinHat_dilate_covariance_uncond`. It changes only
  the REPRESENTATION of the covariance, not its content. **Why (rung 6)**: the covariance is proven in
  `dilateTest` (rational-scale) form, whereas the real-scale continuity foundation
  (`mellinHat_scale_split`) and the capstone's approximating sequence `q_k → c` live in `dilateTestR` form;
  this stages the covariance in the exact shape the real-scale limit consumes — `mellinHat φ` replaced by
  `q_kⁿ⁺¹·mellinHat(dilateTestR (ofQ q_k) φ)` at every rational `q_k`. **Honest scope**: the rational-scale
  covariance re-expressed only — NO real-scale covariance (that is the capstone), NO factorization, NO
  half-line assembly, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4 (band-coupling positivity) is RH;
  crux `none`.

- **The real power `xᵏ` is base-Lipschitz on a bounded domain** (new `Analysis/RpowBaseLip.lean`): for
  real `x, y` with `|x|, |y| ≤ B` (rational `B ≥ 0`), the iterated real power obeys

      `|xᵏ⁺¹ − yᵏ⁺¹| ≤ (k+1)·Bᵏ · |x − y|`

  (`Rpow_base_lip`). The standard telescoping estimate `xⁿ − yⁿ = (x − y)·Σ xⁱyⁿ⁻¹⁻ⁱ`, as an induction:
  the abs-bound `|xᵏ| ≤ Bᵏ` (`Rpow_abs_le`, private) plus the mixed-product identity
  `x·Pₓ − y·Pᵧ = x·(Pₓ − Pᵧ) + (x − y)·Pᵧ` (`mixed_id`, private) give the step
  `|xᵏ⁺² − yᵏ⁺²| ≤ B·((k+1)·Bᵏ·|x−y|) + |x−y|·Bᵏ⁺¹ = (k+2)·Bᵏ⁺¹·|x−y|`. **Why (rung 6)**: the real-scale
  dilation covariance capstone approximates `c` by rationals `q_k → c`, and the outer polynomial factor
  `cⁿ⁺¹` must be shown close to `q_kⁿ⁺¹` at the rate `|c − q_k|` — this supplies exactly that (`B = S`,
  exponent `n+1`, `(n+1)·Sⁿ·|c − q_k|`), the companion of the Mellin scale-continuity
  `mellinHat_scale_split`. **Honest scope**: a general Bishop-real base-Lipschitz bound only — NO
  covariance, NO factorization, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4 (band-coupling positivity)
  is RH; crux `none`.

- **The Mellin transform is scale-continuous (split-at-depth bound)** (new `Square/MellinHatScaleCont.lean`):
  the integer-point Mellin transform `mellinHat (dilateTestR c φ) n = ∫₀^∞ φ(c·x)·xⁿ dx` varies
  continuously in the real dilation scale `c`. For every schedule depth `j`,

      `|mellinHat (dilateTestR c φ) n − mellinHat (dilateTestR c' φ) n|`
      `      ≤ (φ.L + Σ_{m<N_j} φ.L·(m+2)·(powWinTest m n).M)·|c − c'| + 4/(j+1)`,   `N_j = digammaMidx (C·2ⁿ) j`

  (`mellinHat_scale_split`). `mellinHat = mellinMoment + twTail`: the compact moment is `φ.L`-Lipschitz in
  the scale (`mellinMoment_scale_lipschitz`), the tail obeys the split-at-depth bound
  (`twTail_scale_split`); `Rsub_Radd_Radd` + `Rabs_Radd` split `mellinHat(c) − mellinHat(c')` into the
  moment and tail differences and `Rmul_distrib_right` factors the common `|c−c'|`. As `j → ∞`, `c' → c`
  the bound → 0. This is the full Mellin scale-continuity engine the real-scale dilation covariance
  capstone consumes — the rational-scale covariance (`mellinHat_dilate_covariance_uncond`, read in
  `dilateTestR` form by `mellinHat_bridge`) passed to the limit `q_k → c`. **Honest scope**: the
  split-at-depth scale-continuity estimate for the Mellin transform only — NO real-scale covariance (that
  is the capstone), NO factorization, NO half-line assembly, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux.
  Step 4 (band-coupling positivity) is RH; crux `none`.

- **The twisted tail is scale-continuous (split-at-depth bound)** (new `Square/TwTailScaleCont.lean`):
  the twisted tail `twTail (dilateTestR c φ) n` varies continuously in the real dilation scale `c`. For
  every schedule depth `j`,

      `|twTail (dilateTestR c φ) n − twTail (dilateTestR c' φ) n|`
      `      ≤ (Σ_{m<N_j} φ.L·(m+2)·(powWinTest m n).M)·|c − c'| + 4/(j+1)`,   `N_j = digammaMidx (C·2ⁿ) j`

  (`twTail_scale_split`). As `j → ∞` and `c' → c` the right-hand side → 0, so the tail is continuous in
  the scale. **No uniform-in-scale decay hypothesis is needed**: `twTail (dilate_c φ) n` is the `Rlim` of
  the finite partial sums, and the `j`-th partial sum is within `2/(j+1)` of that `Rlim` by the abstract
  Bishop-completeness rate (`Rabs_dist_Rlim`) — a bound uniform in the scale `c` — so the tail remainders
  of the two `twTail`s are each `≤ 2/(j+1)` with no extra hypothesis; the middle finite-head difference is
  the committed `genSum_twTerm_scale_lipschitz`, assembled by a three-term triangle. The per-window
  constant growing with `m` is irrelevant — the tail beyond depth `j` is controlled by the limit rate,
  not by summing the per-window bounds. **Honest scope**: the split-at-depth tail-continuity estimate only
  — NO compact+tail assembly (that is `mellinHat`), NO real-scale covariance, NO factorization, NO
  half-line assembly, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO crux. Step 4 (band-coupling positivity) is RH;
  crux `none`.

- **Tendsto ⟹ per-index real closeness, and its Lipschitz image** (new `Analysis/RTendsToClose.lean`):
  two general Bishop-real convergence primitives. `RTendsTo X L` is a sequence-level predicate
  (`∀ k n, |X_k.seq n − L.seq n| ≤ 2/(k+1) + 2/(n+1)`); `RTendsTo_imp_close` reads off the real statement
  it implies — `|X_k − L| ≤ 2/(k+1)` as a real number, for every `k` (the tendsto bound at the doubled
  index `2n+1`, then `2/(2n+2) ≤ 2/(n+1)`). `Rlip_close` composes this with a real Lipschitz bound: the
  Lipschitz image of a convergent sequence is close to the image of the limit,
  `|g(X_k) − g(L)| ≤ K·(2/(k+1))`. **Why (rung 6)**: the real-scale covariance capstone needs
  `mellinHat (dilate_{q_k} φ) → mellinHat (dilate_c φ)` as `q_k → c` — a Lipschitz map preserving limits —
  which splits into (i) the Lipschitz image is close to the image-of-limit at the scaled rate `K·2/(k+1)`
  (built here, no index acceleration) and (ii) converting that closeness back into `RTendsTo` at the
  canonical rate, which needs a `K`-index reindex (`RmulK`/`Ridx`-style) and is NOT built here.
  **Honest scope**: two convergence primitives only — NO `RTendsTo` of a Lipschitz image (the reindex half
  is unbuilt), NO scale continuity, NO covariance, NO factorization, NO positivity, NO determinacy, NO
  crux. Step 4 (band-coupling positivity) is RH; crux `none`.

- **The rational↔real dilation bridge for the Mellin transform** (new `Square/DilateTestBridge.lean`):
  at a rational scale `q`, the rational-scale dilation `dilateTest q φ` and the real-scale dilation
  `dilateTestR (ofQ q) φ` have LITERALLY IDENTICAL values (`.f x = φ.f (Rmul (ofQ q) x)` for both),
  differing only in their Lipschitz-modulus field (`φ.L·q` vs `φ.L·S`); since the certified Mellin
  objects depend only on the integrand values (certificate independence), the two representations give
  the same moment, the same twisted tail, and the same transform:

      `mellinMoment (dilateTest q φ) n = mellinMoment (dilateTestR (ofQ q) φ) n`   (`mellinMoment_bridge`)
      `twTail      (dilateTest q φ) n = twTail      (dilateTestR (ofQ q) φ) n`   (`twTail_bridge`)

Initial research base for the 𝔽₁-square / Riemann Hypothesis program.

### Added

  carry their established status (`universallyValid := some true`); the RH crux (the
  Hodge index theorem) is encoded as not-asserted (`universallyValid := none`) and is

    verification ladder.

- Repository infrastructure: `README.md`, `CITATION.cff`, this changelog, `.gitignore`,

### Notes

  solution: the formalization compiles and states the construction problem precisely; it

changelog.text:
# Changelog

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and
the version axes are the ones SPEC.md §30.1 separates: the compiler crate and
binary carry the SemVer below, each project selects the supported language
identifier (`1.0`, `1.1`, or `1.2`), and each language's compiler-semantics ID is a
digest over its normative language data, schemas, and pinned golden fixtures.

SPEC.md §2.3 fixes `0.1.0` as the initial implementation version and `1.0.0` as
the first release satisfying the complete specification. No tag before `1.0.0`
is therefore a §30 release: `cargo xtask release-check` reads the complete
§30.3 artifact set and §30.4 completion criterion and refuses, naming every
criterion that does not hold. That refusal is the accurate answer at these
versions. `v0.1.0` is tagged, and `v0.4.0` is tagged at the commit that carries
this changelog; the sections for `0.1.1`, `0.2.0`, and `0.3.0` record what the
workspace carried at those versions without a tag.

## 0.4.0

Release `0.4.0` is cut at the downstream boundary (#92, 2026-10-25): what the
downstream projects need, language 1.2 and the 1.1→1.2 migration (#257), with
everything else that had landed on `release/v0.4` at `201519a1b`, and the
release-workflow fixes and the one self-hosting landing (#298, H5) that reached
the line while the tag waited on them. The register is 457 IDs; the language-1.2
compiler-semantics ID is
`1427f8b629013648a480454d67202788f2303f5396f1d7c70a7c350ddab6f694`, language
1.1's `cac35ee3f026aa21a6c8cbc61f3af3c760da0b94555876a4540cc235f461bfdb`, and
language 1.0's `07859acb5a756221018b7f65e7f725d99b00a694670eecc7cd264832ba1333fb`.
Of the compiler's own pipeline as language-1.2 source (#92), this release ships
exactly the stages the register carries: `BS-01` to `BS-06` and `BS-09`. Of the
Rust runtime as source (#91), it ships the heap half through H5: `RB-15` to
`RB-17`, `RB-19` to `RB-21`, `SP-21` to `SP-23`, and `SP-25` to `SP-29`. The Rust
lowering as source (`BS-07`, `BS-08`, `BS-10` to `BS-14`), the number functions of
the std runtime as machine calls with their refinement theorems (H6), and the H7
audit are written and land in `0.4.1` on the same line, each with its identity
regeneration; the remaining self-hosting steps are `0.5.0` material. Also in
`0.4.1`, not here: the seven example retitles (#251) and the four negative
fixtures for `LLB6005`, `LLB6006`, `LLB6007`, and `LLT4016` (#252), so at this tag
those four refusals are evidenced by inline conformance cases only, and the
negative-fixture bullet of #34 is not met for them. The language-model rows are
`LM-01` to `LM-09` and `LM-13`. Nothing below claims more than the certificates
of this tree show.

- The release workflow's evidence is the gate run of the tagged commit (SPEC.md
  §9.4, §30.3; `RP-18`). `release.yml` no longer runs `just vv` on one runner:
  rehearsals 3 and 4 showed the `bdd` recipe alone takes over four hours there
  and the job hits the six-hour limit before Atlas. `.github/release-gate.sh`
  finds the `ci.yml` run that was the whole gate on the commit's tree (the
  commit, or the second parent of a merge that lands its tree unchanged, as
  `ci-plan.sh` reads a push), requires every job of it to have passed with the
  Atlas join, every host, and every leg present, and writes `vv-evidence.txt`
  with the run, its jobs, and the legs' retained transcripts. `conformance_rp_18`
  requires the gate job to run the script and no recipe, and runs the script
  against planted runs: a run with a failed job, a draft run, and no run are
  refused, and a run on the tree-equal parent is accepted. The first tag run
  (40321415513, on `aa6593e02`) then failed at `release-check`: the §30.3
  criterion reads the line `just vv` prints when the whole gate passes, and
  the legs' transcripts never say it. The script now ends the file with that
  line as the summary of the run, the criterion is one function
  (`repo_model::release::ci_evidence`) with its own test, and `RP-18` holds
  the script's output to it, so the publish job, which no rehearsal runs,
  cannot refuse what the rehearsals accepted.
- `lexlean migrate --to 1.2 [--check]`, #257 (SPEC.md §17.12, §23.4,
  `CL-24`): the one command that migrates a language-1.1 data-form project to
  language 1.2. It rewrites every module to the authoring notation through
  `lexlean::sdk::to_notation`, moves the builtin glossary references of the
  sources and the imports of every path lexicon package to `1.2.0`, rewrites the
  `language` row, and regenerates the lock as `lexlean/lock/2`, after proving
  the result in a scratch copy; a refusal (`LLC0103`, `LLP2003`, or the check's
  own diagnostic) writes nothing. The `1.1` to `1.2` recipe of §17.12 (change
  the tag and the glossary versions, relock) is replaced: it produced a project
  that language 1.2 refuses with `LLP2003` since #149. The negative fixture
  `migrate-module-without-notation` holds a module that is not a language-1.1
  module (a top-level member the schema forbids), which the notation cannot
  spell. A file that changes between the proof and the replacement refuses the
  migration (`LLV7010`), and a replacement that fails restores every file
  already replaced and reports every restore that failed. A refusal creates no
  build root, and a data form that is not canonical JSON (which language 1.1
  `check` refuses with `LLT4001`) is refused with `LLP2003` and not
  canonicalized.
  `Engine` keeps its seven entry points; the function is
  `lexlean::api::migrate::migrate`. The register is 453 IDs. The notation
  reader no longer takes a keyword followed by `{` inside a parenthesised term
  for the keyword's own form: a `match` (or `not`, `first`, `second`, `cons`,
  `nil`, ...) that a readable form cannot carry, such as one holding a variable
  named `first`, is printed generically (SPEC.md §17.21.1) and now reads back.
- The `lexlean` crate that goes to crates.io is the crate the release attaches (`RP-18`, #260). `.github/workflows/crate.yml`, which `release.yml` calls on every run, packages the crate twice to the same bytes, runs `cargo publish --dry-run`, checks the archive for what crates.io needs (description, license, repository, the readme it names, at most 10 MiB), and compares its SHA-256 with `release/lexlean.crate` and the line `checksums.txt` lists for it; the tag's `publish` job repeats the comparison against the dry-run package and uploads to crates.io only when a `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret or trusted publishing (the repository variable `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING`) authorises it, and otherwise creates the release and says the crate was not uploaded, where before the first run failed after the tag was pushed because no `lexlean` crate and no trusted publisher existed. Dispatched on a `release/vX.Y` line, `crate.yml` does the same for the pre-release `X.Y.0-dev.N`, `N` being the commit's number of first-parent commits, and uploads it under the same authority. The decisions are in `.github/crate-publication.sh`, which the case runs against planted archives, checksums, refs and environments. SPEC.md §30.3 states the rule. Register 449.

- The Rust runtime as source, #91 stage 4 (SPEC.md §17.16, §17.17, `SP-21`,
  `RB-15`, `SP-23`, `SM-35`, `SM-36`, `RB-16`, `SP-22`, `RB-17`, `SP-25`, `RB-19`, `BS-09`, `SP-26`, `SP-27`, `SP-28`, `SP-29`, `RB-20`).
  The declared Rust machine grows by the primitives the runtime is written in
  (the bit operations, the natural and integer comparisons and remainders, the
  checked natural and integer arithmetic that is `Some` or `None` on overflow)
  and the Rust AST by the machine callee and the overflow value. Language 1.2
  gains `term_cases` and `cases` on a Boolean as proof forms. The core
  runtime's 110 numeric functions are the definitions of the module
  `RustRuntime` (`coreCrate`), decoded and printed in place of the handwritten
  text and held to it by a differential and to `RustSemantics` by a
  `refines_<path>` theorem each; its support items (`use`, `Overflow`, the
  work counter, the traits `Same` and `Key` and their impls, `equal`,
  `compare`) are the definitions of `RuntimeSupport`, a crate of the second
  closed module `RuntimeSyntax`, checked by a validator of 24 named rules, with
  the meaning of `equal` and `compare` stated by `RuntimeSemantics` and proved
  against the calculus primitives for the core profile's scalars and pairs of
  two scalars (nested keys are validated, not proved: #249). The handwritten
  base text is gone. The
  compiler-semantics ID moves; records bound to it regenerate once, at the
  landing. `RB-19` adds the constructs of the heap runtime (40 validator rules, sixteen new): every name the printer writes is an identifier and not a keyword, a derive is in a closed table of five, a character literal is one scalar value, the head of a condition holds no struct literal outside parentheses, and a `let`, cast or type argument names no generic parameter; each site is planted, and a comparison whose left operand ends in a cast is printed with parentheses. `BS-09` holds the runtime validator's Lean twin (`RuntimeValidate`, a bootstrap root) to the Rust oracle. The twin carries the identifier, derive, character-literal, struct-head and type-scope rules of `RB-19` (40 rules), and the bootstrap project's `max_file_bytes` is 6 MiB because its certificate passed 4 MiB. The committed corpus `BS-05` and `BS-06` hold to the oracle grows by the `validate_runtime` package (256 manifests, 173 programs, 232 crates; 466 and 329 validator runs, 622 printer runs), and `validate_runtime` has its stack bound in `tests/stack-bounds.json`. `SP-26` kernel-checks the laws of the memory a runtime buffer lives in (`RustMemory`). `SP-27` kernel-checks the abstraction theorems of the list representation (`RustLists`). `SP-28` states the meaning of the buffer, share, and replace primitives over that model (`RustPrims`). `SP-29` and `RB-20` carry the list, byte, and text functions of the `rust-std` runtime, `append_list`, `length_list`, `index_list`, `slice_list`, `append_bytes`, `length_bytes`, `length_string`, `index_bytes`, `slice_bytes`, `utf8_encode`, `utf8_decode`, `compare_bytes`, `split_exact` and `join`, as source: the module `RustStd` defines each as one machine call (`Machine.listAppend` to `stringJoin`, families 26 to 39, whose meaning `RustSemantics` states as the calculus primitive of the runtime item of the same function), `refines_<function>` is kernel-checked against the run of the runtime item, the std text is the handwritten base with the generated functions in place of their oracle functions, and a differential with counted work holds them to the oracle. The shipped crate gains `Type::Param`, the fourteen machine families, and the decoder of the std module; the bootstrap project's `max_file_bytes` is 6 MiB; the library audit reads the std text as generated. `RB-20` also prints the types, impls, and helpers of the std runtime (`Str`, `Bytes`, `Node`, `Repr`, `List`, `chars`, and the `Same` and `Key` impls) from a second module, `RuntimeStd`, decoded, checked by the validator of `RuntimeSyntax` with the support items, and printed in place of the handwritten text. The runtime validator (`RB-19`) learns the associated function of a declared type, which the Lean twin (`BS-09`, now 703 crates) follows, the printer writes `x = x + e` as `x += e` (the package's lint gate refuses the first), and the library table lists the paths the printed text uses (`Rc::from`, `mem::replace`, `str::from_utf8`, and `pop`). With the number text (`canonical_decimal`, `parse_int`, the eight `format_`/`parse_` pairs) in `RuntimeStd`, no handwritten runtime text remains: the oracle at `tests/rust-runtime-oracle/` is replaced by a golden transcript (`tests/rust-runtime-golden/transcript.txt`, a 64-bit digest of the results and counted work of the calls under each label, recorded from the handwritten runtime at the last pass of the differential), and `RB-21` refuses any string literal of the `lexlean` sources that holds the head of a runtime item. The register is 457 IDs.
- Two source packages of the standard library and the application that uses
  them, #32 (SPEC.md §17.22, §10.5, `SL-03`, `SL-04`, `EX-09`). `std-models`
  (`LexLeanStdModels.Scores`) holds the score combinators `best`, `margin`, and
  `decideOr` over `List Int` and the contract `Gating`, realization `Gate`,
  evidence `GateEvidence`, and model `GateModel` generic over a type parameter;
  `std-reasoning` (`LexLeanStdReasoning.Worklist`) holds the generic logic
  `Countdown`, its rules `Tick` and `Burn`, the verifier `Drained`, and the
  terminating work-list reasoner `Drain`. Both are workspace members that an
  importer pins, hold their laws as kernel-checked theorems, and claim no
  differential: language 1.2 is generic over types and not over predicates or
  stages, so neither offers a composite that takes the importer's models
  (SPEC.md §17.22 says so). `examples/helpdesk` imports them and `stdlib`: its
  roots `classify` (the model alone), `plan` (the reasoner alone), and
  `dispatch : Bytes -> Bytes` (both) are exported through the production
  consumer, the packages committed under `tests/production-export/helpdesk/`.
  The workspace file lists the three new members. No language data or schema
  moves, so no language-1.2 record other than the new projects' own is
  regenerated. The register is 436 IDs.
- The audit of certificate A checks a mutual group of implementation records
  (`f._unsafe_rec`) by the union of the sets it prints for the group, against a
  pin that is the group's union (SPEC.md §17.17, `LLV7013` names the group).
  What Lean prints of one member is not a property of its term alone: it
  stores axiom data by one shared traversal in the order of a hash map keyed by
  names that carry the identity, so the first member of the bootstrap project's
  R6 group, `__fits_76`, pinned `[]` row by row and printing `[]` on main's
  identity only by that order, printed `[propext]` on others with identical
  sources.
  The pin and the check now state the same order-independent set. Found by the
  slice 3 identity (#221).
- Text classifiers, composition, and adapters, and the audit that no prompt is
  code (SPEC.md §17.12, *Text components* rules 8 to 10, `LM-07`..`LM-09`,
  slice 3 of #30; no new code). A `text_classifier` over a prior tokenizer and
  a prior stateless `list int` model whose evidence discharges every runtime
  check elaborates to `features` (the count of each token id below the
  tokenizer's `size`), `classifyTokens` (the model applied to the features), and
  `classify` over `string` through `encodeText`, and generates
  `features_width` (exactly `size` entries), `features_total` (the features of
  an encoded text sum to its token count, so no token is dropped), and
  `features_fit` (`fitWidth`, the fixed-width map a linear or neural stage
  needs to apply to an arbitrary `list int`, leaves them unchanged); the
  declaration gains an `axioms` policy. A stateful model that steps by a
  window's `push` composes under `scan`, its `satisfies_contract` evidence
  proved by the window's generated `push_bounded`, and an adapter is a model
  over `string` whose realization applies `classify` or `generate` and whose
  evidence the generated laws prove, so the declaration kinds are those of
  before. The audit walks the primitive registry, the production registry, and
  the text declarations of the closed schema and refuses an operation that
  takes a `string` or `bytes` operand and returns anything but data, a registry
  that names an operation the other does not, and a free string member of a
  text declaration. The classifier's functions and laws are new declarations
  of the native `LexLeanText` module, authored once outside the release tree
  and exported by the same round trip as the earlier slices
  (`tests/text-laws/MIGRATION.md`, third record). The language-1.2 `semantic_ir`
  and `latex_backend` versions move to 15 and 14, and the schema
  `semantic-module-v2` gives `text_classifier` an `axioms` member, so every
  language-1.2 lock, golden, fixture, and verification record is regenerated
  with the maintainer's wave. Production (`text_rows`), `rust-std` and
  `rust-core`, and the end-to-end example are not part of this change. The
  register holds 433 IDs.
- Context windows and text generators (SPEC.md §17.12, *Text components*,
  `LM-04`..`LM-06`, slice 2 of #30; new code `LLT4016`). A `context_window`
  of capacity at least 1 and overflow `refuse` or `keep_last` elaborates to
  `capacity`, `fit`, and `push` over the text-laws library and generates
  `bounded`, `push_bounded`, `exact`, and `suffix` (`keep_last`) or
  `refuses` (`refuse`). A `text_generator` over a prior tokenizer, window,
  stateless `list uint32 -> list int` model, and `uint32` stop token, with
  `max_tokens` at least 1, elaborates to `score`, the closed inductives
  `End` (`stop`, `exhausted`) and `Failure` (`unknown_token`,
  `context_overflow`, `invalid_utf8`), `run` (the library's bounded loop),
  `generateTokens`, and `generate`, and generates `bounded` (at most
  `max_tokens` tokens) and `context_bounded` (the scorer is never consulted
  on a context that does not fit). `greedy` takes the first maximum and no
  seed; `sample` draws through the closed `xorshift32` and `proportional`
  members with the seed an explicit input and the next seed an explicit
  output. Both declarations gain an `axioms` policy. A capacity or
  `max_tokens` of 0 is `LLT4016`; a member of another kind is `LLT4006`. The
  laws are new declarations of the native `LexLeanText` module, authored once
  outside the release tree and exported by the same round trip as slice 1
  (`tests/text-laws/MIGRATION.md`, second record). The language-1.2
  `semantic_ir` and `latex_backend` versions move to 14 and 13, so every
  language-1.2 lock, golden, fixture, and verification record is
  regenerated. Text classifiers, adapters, composition, production, and the
  end-to-end example are not part of this change. The register holds 429 IDs.
- The repository's own URL is `https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/LexLean`
  (#34, D1): the `repository` and `homepage` fields of the workspace manifest,
  SPEC.md §1 and §2.3, the README, the image's `org.opencontainers.image.source`
  label, and the `$id` of every schema under `schemas/`, `api/schemas/` and
  `tooling/schemas/` name the organization. The schema identifiers are inputs
  of every language's compiler-semantics ID, so every identity moves; the
  records bound to them are regenerated in this wave. The five API schemas
  keep their spec versions: `api/schemas/versions.toml` records their new
  digests, since only the host in their `$id` changed, not the contract
  (`PX-12`).
- Language 1.2 refuses the data form, #149 (SPEC.md §17.11, §17.21.1,
  `AU-13`). A module that states `\semanticdata{…}`, `\toolingdata{…}` or
  `\coredata{…}` is refused with `LLP2003` at its data argument, naming the
  notation; `fmt` no longer rewrites such a module, and
  `lexlean::sdk::to_notation` / `to_data_form` are the explicit conversion
  (§24.8). Languages 1.0 and 1.1 and the Atlas are unchanged. `AU-02`, `AU-05`
  and `AU-10` no longer compare a build of the data form with the notation (it
  is not a language-1.2 source) and their statements say what they check. The
  language-1.2 records are regenerated in the milestone's one wave, not here.
  `AU-13` brings the register to 415 IDs.
- Certificate B certifies a function the renderer writes as a loop (`SP-20`,
  SPEC.md §17.17, stage 4 of #91): `FunOK` is now the disjunction of `FunOK0`
  (the statement it was) and `FunLoop`, that the crate's body is the library's
  `loopOf` of an ordinary recursive body, its Boolean checks closed by
  evaluation, with the correspondence of that recursive body; `funSem_loop`
  proves the simulation from the recursive body's, and `funSem_of` has one arm
  more. `Corr`, its recursor, and `sound` are untouched. The aligner reads a
  loop back into its recursive body (`data_b/loopform.rs`) and refuses, as
  *Certificate B rejected*, a loop that is not the form of any. 198 authored
  declarations (900 rows with their derived ones) are added to the preservation library (tests/preservation-library/
   MIGRATION.md). The new library needs the decoder fix of #212 (a compiled
  mutual group is never split across commands). The language-1.2 compiler-semantics ID moves
  again; the records bound to it are regenerated by the maintainer, not in this
  change.
- The declared Rust machine states a loop over a state with a break value
  (`SP-19`, SPEC.md §17.16, stage 3 of #91): `RustSyntax.Expr.loop` names a
  state and a body block, and `RustSemantics` runs the body, rebinds the state
  on `Ok`, and ends with the payload of `Err`, recursing through `eval` so that
  the mutual group and the statement of `stable` are unchanged. The renderer
  prints it, the validator checks that the body moves only the state, and the
  moves pass and the certificate-B term builder have a case for it. Twelve
  authored declarations of the preservation library are repaired by kernel-term
  edits and one lemma, `stable_loop`, is added (tests/preservation-library/
  MIGRATION.md). The tail-recursive templates lower to it since `RB-14`
  (#105 step 2, below). The language-1.2 compiler-semantics ID moves again; the
  records bound to it are regenerated by the maintainer, not in this change.
- Tail-recursive library templates render as loops (`RB-14`, SPEC.md §17.13,
  §17.16, #105 step 2): a function whose self calls are all tail calls is
  rendered as a `loop` over its accumulator that breaks with its result, so its
  row carries no `recursion`; nine rows of `language/production-1.2.toml` and
  nineteen declarations of the examples, the standard library and the bootstrap
  project lose the effect, a rendering that states a self call where a loop is
  possible is refused, and the printer binds a loop body's value before its
  `match`. `validate::CORRESPONDENCE` admits `expr:call` as an origin of the
  pair and result constructs a loop's state and break carry, for any call of
  the program (the coarsening is stated in SPEC.md §17.16). The language-1.2
  compiler-semantics ID moves; the records bound to it are regenerated in wave 6.
  In the same wave the declarations of `scanSource`, `rejectAtoms`, `sha256`
  and `sha256Hex` drop `recursion` (`BS-03` and `SL-02` hold a declaration to
  exactly the realized effects), and the stack-bounds record of `PD-08` is
  re-measured for the three packages that still recurse, `parse_audit_output`,
  `check_program` and `check_arguments`, with the growth table moved from
  `isClosedLeanName`, now a loop, to `parseAuditOutput` on one audit output of
  a growing number of records; `BS-04` records or demands the bounds of the
  two checkers as `BS-01` does the parser's.
- The declared Rust machine states a machine primitive as a callee and the
  overflow value as a literal (`SP-18`, SPEC.md §17.16, stage 2 of #91):
  `RustSyntax.Machine` has eight primitives at a width, `Callee.machine`
  names one, and `Lit.overflow` is the unit struct `Overflow`; `RustSemantics`
  evaluates a machine call as the calculus primitive of the same name. The five
  authored declarations of the preservation library that this leaves a case
  short (`stable`, `rc_call_function`, `rc_call_runtime`, `rc_call_halt`,
  `rc_negate`) are repaired by kernel-term edits, and the library's derived
  rows are made by Lean for the new modules. The renderer writes neither
  construct (#105 step 2 lowers to them). The language-1.2 compiler-semantics ID moves again; the
  records bound to it are regenerated by the maintainer, not in this change.
- The decoder of derived rows refuses a module in which a derived sparse
  `casesOn` is referred to by the type or value of no row (`SM-34`): a recipe
  is checked by its uses, and SM-34 states that a recipe naming other valid
  constructors where the use accepts them is not distinguished.
- Derived rows leave the preservation library's sources (`SM-34`, SPEC.md
  §17.10, the prerequisite of #91 stage 2). A row of `lexlean/core-module/2`
  may be derived: it states its name, kind, and extension state, and for a
  sparse `casesOn` its recipe, and no universe parameters, type, or value; the
  decoder makes the constant with the pinned Lean's own construction at the
  row's place in the order and refuses the module unless the construction makes
  it. The notation writes such a row without a type. The 13 modules of the
  preservation library state their 6,890 reserved-name rows and 313 sparse
  `casesOn` rows as derived rows, and the nodes nothing else reaches are gone
  (1,096,114 to 744,450). A stored row keeps decoding as before, so the
  Atlas, the runtime and certification libraries, and every committed
  certificate E are unchanged. Language 1.2's compiler-semantics ID moves with
  the library and the schema; the records bound to it are regenerated by the
  maintainer, not in this change.
- Certificate A of lists of recursive types (#208, `SP-15`): a record or
  inductive holding a `List` of a recursive type as a root parameter, `cons`
  onto such a list, and a closure whose boundary encoders were split across
  64-declaration commands are certified. A bundle a compiled row applies is
  compiled; a nested list's payload in `construct_cons` is its items row; a
  safe mutual group of compiled rows is one scheduling node and never split
  across commands. `lean_backend` moves to `21` (language 1.2): the
  language-1.2 compiler-semantics ID moves, and with it the lock, source,
  semantic, and build IDs of every 1.2 project, to be regenerated with the
  identity wave. `SP-15` is its own part of `bdd`.
- A lowered program nested beyond `PROGRAM_JSON_DEPTH` (512 arrays and objects)
  is refused with `LLS8002` in phase lowering, where `Program::to_file_bytes`

  - a declaration of its module;
  - a built-in name the backend emits;

  - the canonical LaTeX states the type parameters of parameterized data;
  - every declaration is its own source-map node in both artifacts;

  arguments, a constructor mismatch, and a forward reference.

  explicit captures, full applications, definition references, and generic

  non-escaping closures and executable callees: no type they state or write
  may hold a function, directly or through a document type's fields, and a
  function parameter is used only where a closure may be. Type parameters
  never capture a backend type, a document type, or a value binder, and the

  `SemanticSnapshot::alpha_ids`. Fifteen new negative fixtures cover
  capture, arity, typing, escaping closures (returned, stored in an

  Changes after review:
  - Binder hygiene (§17.12 rule 10) covers generic type parameters and

    declaration, nor the module prefix can be captured.

  well-founded call may sit under `if` and `match`: its obligation is

  measure, the pruning under binders its branches ignore). The new `linear_arithmetic` proof form

  referenced as a value, a mutual label shared by an inductive and a
  definition group) is rejected; eleven new negative fixtures cover these
  and the decrease and evidence rules (`DF-16`, `DF-17`, `PF-19`, `SM-27`).
  Changes after review:

  - The example adds a structural mutual constant-folding rewriter over

  - `SM-28` and `SM-30` check every operation, under Lean, against an

  production compilation. It is defined as LexLean in the new `compiler/`

  `lexlean::calculus`, provides:

  - the static rules, failing closed with the new `LLB6005`;
  - a reference interpreter;
  - a realization library that transcribes every collection primitive;
  - a realization table covering every runtime construct of the production

  - the reference Rust rendering under `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

  The hand-constructed fixtures are confirmed three ways: Lean's kernel (or,

  Changes after review:
  - The step count charges every operation the evaluator performs: the
    bindings a lookup examines, each arm a match tries, the captures an
    application passes, the fields a projection skips, and a primitive's
    operand and result weights (one per node, plus characters and bytes).

  closed Rust AST (`lexlean::calculus::rust::ast`) and checked before it is
  printed into canonical bytes:
  - identifiers are generated from closed kinds, and each is bound once per
    function;
  - every value is moved at most once;

  - failure is typed exactly: a function that can overflow returns `R<T>`
    and every call to it propagates, and any other returns its value;
  - every construct carries the calculus element it was lowered from, and
    is refused unless its correspondence row names that element, at that
    element's width, and the program uses it.

  Unicode tables. A type no value inhabits is rendered as an empty match

  - the comparison boundary;

    selectors over shared plans) with definitional completeness evidence;
  - the scalar or componentwise (steps, size) order;
  - the claim class and its scope.

  rejected, as are hidden costs, unrealizable actions, and claims over the
  wrong order or beyond the grammar. An unknown cost leaves the answer

  `inference_rule`, `verifier`, and `reasoner` declarations and the
  `reasoning_failure` type, in the closed `lexlean/semantic-module/2`
  schema, with no oracle, prompt, or reasoner primitive. Each elaborates in
  linking to ordinary inductives, structures, definitions, and theorems over
  `match`, `if`, `list_fold`, `iterate_until`, and set primitives.
  - Rules are guarded transitions of a logic's state with statement-exact
    soundness and progress theorems; verifiers are executable checks with
    exact soundness (and completeness) theorems; reasoners are `forward`
    (first applicable rule in priority and candidate order, under fuel),
    `search` (breadth- or depth-first under fuel and a frontier bound,
    optionally deduplicating over an ordered state type), or
    `generate_and_verify` (a generator's candidates checked in order within a
    mandatory budget). Logics, rules, verifiers, and reasoners may be

    `observation_invariant` (a predicate of the observation and a state kept
    by every step), and `answer_correct` (the answer term correct on every
    state, or on every state satisfying the invariant or the observation
    invariant, which erases the check).
  - Verdicts are the verifier-accepted (or proved-correct) answer or one of
    `exhausted`, `unsolved`, `rejected`, `invalid_step`; a forward reasoner
    answers only from a saturated state. Traces are `E.Step` data, evidence
    only by replay. A six-counter ledger (iterations, guard evaluations,
    firings, expansions, verifications, frontier peak) accounts every run.
  - Generated theorems are fixed-template applications of the formal-only,
    axiom-free `LexLeanReasoning` runtime and are restated by pinned Lean;

    title glossary) with the six-counter ledger of each run decided by the
    kernel; 85 new negative fixtures; the `compiler` project's five oracle
    modules (`ReasoningOracle`, `GradeOracle`, `BudgetOracle`,
    `PlannerOracle`, `ScreeningOracle`) stating every reasoner the example's
    production roots run, with calculus transcriptions of each strategy
    (the forward engines `Triage`, `Review`, `Grade`, and the generic
    `Spend`; the breadth-first search with deduplication `Plan`; the
    depth-first search `Screen`; the generate-and-verify `Dose`) and their
    rust-core and rust-std packages, in the new `ReasoningFixtures` module;
    GNAF requests over forward-chaining plans, each plan tied to the
    oracle's `Triage` on the request's domain.
  - `answer_correct` names a theorem of one of three exact statements: the
    answer correct on every state (`forall x s v, a = some v -> Spec x v`),
    on every state satisfying the logic's invariant (`forall x s v, J s -> a
    = some v -> Spec x v`, which needs the `initial_invariant` claim and
    whose premise the generated run theorem `E.run_invariant` discharges),
    or on every state a new `observation_invariant` claim holds of
    (`forall x s v, Rl x s -> a = some v -> Spec x v`, where `Rl : (I, S) ->
    prop` holds of the observed state and is kept by the logic's relation,
    so `Spec` may depend on the observation: `Grade` answers a chart's level,
    at most 3 and 3 only for a hypotensive patient). The check of a reasoner
    that claims any form is erased in its own verdict, but only an answer
    correct on every state may be read by executable code without its
    verifier: under an invariant, `E.extract`, `E.accept`, and `E.conclude`
    (forward) or `E.searchStep` (search) are `LLT4012`, because each reads
    an answer from a state or search the caller supplies.
  - A declaration named like, or below, any namespace the generated Lean
    refers to (`LexLeanReasoning.Star`, but also `Nat.x` or `List.y`) is
    refused in language 1.2 (`LLT4001`): the reservation is not limited to
    reasoning modules.
  - The elaboration charge of a reasoner covers the type arguments of every
    use of its logic, rules, and verifier; it remains a fitted bound checked
    after elaboration, not a proof.
  - Generated bounds also state a forward run's firings and a search's
    verifications and expansions at most the fuel (`E.firings_bounded`,
    `E.verifications_bounded`, `E.expansions_bounded`), recorded in the
    eligibility report; a run's guard evaluations and a search's firings are
    accounted, not bounded.
  - Every logic, rule, verifier, and reasoner is charged to `max_ir_nodes`
    for the most its elaboration can be before it is elaborated
    (`LLS8002`), and the rules of a reasoner are combined as balanced
    trees, so an elaboration nests with the logarithm of its rule count.
  - The language-1.2 `semantic_ir`, `lean_backend`, and `latex_backend`
    versions are bumped; `linear_arithmetic` also rewrites with
    `Bool.and_eq_true`, `Bool.or_eq_true`, `Bool.not_eq_true'`, `and_true`,

    per-root `reasoning` rows, and its schema now admits the model and
    reasoning construct keys. The snapshot elaboration gains `theorems`.

  primitive now admits `recursion` (SPEC.md §17.13, `TC-06`; #105). Those
  primitives are realized by library templates that call themselves, so the
  stack depth of the rendered Rust is bounded only by the input (a scan of an
  80,000-byte name aborted on an 8 MiB stack), yet their registry rows said
  `recursion = false` and no root declared the effect. The rows are corrected,
  and `conformance_tc_06` derives each runtime row's `recursion` from its
  realization (the call graph of a template's instance, or the structural
  `recursion` reference) instead of trusting the row. The language-1.2
  compiler-semantics ID changes with the registry; `examples/reasoning` and
  `examples/production-coverage` declare the effect on the roots that use these
  primitives.
- The host legs of CI may run for 120 minutes, where they were cut off at 60:
  the Intel macOS leg takes 51 to 61 minutes, and a leg cancelled at its limit
  is not a result about the code.
- `conformance_rs_12` no longer reports a slow runner as a different claim
  (#145; test hardening, no compiler change, no new diagnostic code). Its
  planted verification of a copy of the `compiler` project expects Lean to
  refuse the planted transcriptions with `LLV7002`; on four runs a runner
  stall made Lean's children take 5 to 20 times their usual time, one hit
  the 300 s default of `child_timeout_ms`, and the case saw `LLS8002`
  instead. The scratch copy now allows 900 s, so the case again states only
  what Lean said about the planted module. The committed `compiler` project,
  its limits, and `verified_compiler()` are unchanged.
- The start-order case of the verifier pool no longer reads the scheduler
  (#148; test hardening, no compiler change). It recorded the order in which
  four workers ran, not the order in which they claimed their items, and
  failed 82 of 600 runs beside eight busy loops and once on an Intel macOS
  host leg; it now observes the claims through two workers.

## 0.3.0

- Support exhaustive Boolean matches and keep imported list construction
  definitions exposed for kernel reduction across generated modules.
- Preserve digit runs inside `semanticdata` JSON string values as exact string
  content. Exact content identities beginning with zero no longer trigger the
  standalone LexLean numeral canonicalization diagnostic; JSON numeric tokens
  and ordinary source numerals retain their existing leading-zero rejection.
  Payload tracking is linear in source size and respects whitespace, escaped
  quotes, and control-shaped bytes inside strings.
- Treat Lean comment delimiters inside generated string literals as data while
  retaining the backend invariant that generated Lean syntax contains no line
  or block comments.
- Generic language support for production modeling: generic semantic identifier
  quotation for reserved Lean keywords/segments, full Lean string escape sequence
  support without parser divergence, and bounded semantic elaboration for large byte
  constants.
- Immutable typed authority binding and oracle evidence: Lean 4.32.1, Lake,
  leanchecker, and `#print axioms` bound to upstream Lean FRO release 4.32.1, source commit
  `f054605aea4b840552cca2e725580bffd1e1b704`, and archive SHA-256
  `6dec8667fbf57ba480a18a8b0c353b2ee157346b2630b211ccbefeedf20545f8`, with positive
  and negative oracle execution records.
- First-party package identity and publishing bootstrap: owner-controlled initial token
  upload support in release workflow before OIDC trusted publishing transition, and
  standalone offline package verification (`cargo xtask check-package`).
- Release identity provenance and tree manifest package: `release/release-identity.json`
  and `release/MANIFEST.sha256` binding all 712 packaged files, consumed by PrismPM
  without source-only assumptions.

## 0.2.0

Language 1.1 gains the closed portable data and operation vocabulary required
by generated application runtimes. This is the immutable PrismPM integration
line; it does not weaken the separate LexLean 1.0.0 full-spec release gate.

### Implemented

- Distinct mathematical `Int` and fixed-width signed/unsigned integer types,
  UTF-8 strings, byte sequences, ordering, option, and result values, with
  canonical checked literals and no implicit host-width conversion.
- Twenty-eight generic typed operations covering checked arithmetic and
  conversion, quotient/remainder zero cases, bit operations and bounded
  shifts, collections and byte ranges, UTF-8, byte ordering, bounded exact
  split/join, and canonical decimal parse/format.
- One fixed Lean 4.32.1 runtime lowering and canonical LaTeX rendering for the
  portable vocabulary. Definitions and theorems both carry exact observed
  axiom policies; verification still elaborates, replays with `leanchecker`,
  and audits every policy.
- `SM-17` through `SM-22`, an all-operation semantic fixture, exhaustive
  fixed-width bound/signature tests, schema validation, malformed-input cases,
  and cross-root snapshot identity checks. The register now contains 222
  implemented capability IDs.

### Compatibility

- Language 1.0 syntax and meaning are unchanged. Language 1.1 and
  `lexlean/semantic-snapshot/1` are extended in place under the ecosystem's
  pre-freeze policy; their compiler-semantics digest and affected expected
  artifacts are regenerated.
- No Prism-, Holo-, or Calculator-specific node, raw Lean/Rust field, macro,
  tactic, or backend escape hatch is added.

### Not claimed

- This remains an integration release rather than the complete LexLean §30
  release, which is intentionally reserved for version 1.0.0.

## 0.1.1

The UOR Atlas becomes the foundation model of LexLean: every accepted document
carries the Atlas-derived header, and the Atlas formalization is closed inside
the repository.

### Implemented

- The one-time Atlas conversion is closed and recorded in
  `examples/uor-atlas/MIGRATION.md`; its independently authored Lean source and
  exporter are absent from the release tree. `VR-19` now permanently audits
  the native source graph itself: every source module has one generated Lean
  module, public imports stay within `Init` and the generated graph, the only
  backend-support import is `Lean`, and no second Atlas implementation exists.
  `just vv` verifies the generated native Atlas
  under `leanprover/lean4:v4.32.1`, replays it through `leanchecker` — a
  same-kernel replay, not an independent checker (§22.4) — and runs the
  standing exact axiom gate.
- Two new built-in lexicon packages, `lexlean.std.int@1.0.0` and
  `lexlean.uor.atlas@1.0.0`. The Atlas package is registered under
  `[[builtin_package]]`, locked into every project, and unconditionally
  visible in every document, so the header is carried whether or not a
  document names an Atlas entry; its visibility closes transitively over
  `lexlean.core`, `lexlean.std.nat`, and `lexlean.std.int`.
- The frozen Atlas pack is complete against the native source register: every
  label carries exactly one disposition, the registers key on exact
  identifiers, and every frozen entry refers to a declaration owned by the
  native source rather than importing an independently authored module.
  Coverage begins at `Atlas.lex.tex`; exercise, denotation,
  surface-disjointness, and authority-scope audits run as gates,
  each with a planted-defect record in VERIFICATION.md.
- `examples/uor-atlas/` verifies under the pinned toolchain with its
  committed verification records, and the negative fixture suite grows to 28
  classes with `atlas-level-conflation`, rejected by `LLR3005`: a native Atlas
  document declaration cannot be consumed as an external glossary atom.
- `examples/uor-atlas/src/Atlas.lex.tex` is the single native semantic and
  proof source for 5,519 environment declarations; 58 private source-compiler
  implementation records remain hashed provenance and are emitted by neither
  backend. Both backends traverse that closed DAG, generated Lean publicly
  imports only `Init` and generated Atlas modules, privately imports only the
  generic `Lean` support module, and contains no independently authored Atlas
  implementation.
  `S43` is authoritatively the proved integer-uniqueness statement.
  `SM-15` and `VR-19` bring the register to 211 IDs, all implemented at level
  `build`.
- Language `1.1` adds a closed generic semantic declaration, term, and proof
  language for structures, classes, instances, finite inductives, total
  structural recursion, exhaustive matches, Boolean validators, exact theorem
  application, and axiom-free Boolean reflection. Its seven-module
  `semantic-1.1` fixture contains no handwritten Lean and exercises every
  closed variant through elaboration, `leanchecker`, and exact axiom audit.
- The stable seventh `Engine` operation returns an owned, read-only,
  path-independent `lexlean/semantic-snapshot/1` DTO. The public DTOs and
  complete closed JSON Schema expose every legal semantic module variant while
  keeping mutable compiler internals and both fixed backends private. `SM-16`,
  `DF-11`, `CF-16`, `CL-19`, and `CL-20` bring the register to 216 IDs, all
  implemented at level `build`.

### Changed

- Generated-module verification passes Lean an explicit package root with
  `-R`. This removes random staging paths from `.olean` serialization, so a
  same-platform verification has byte-identical oleans and an identical
  attestation across absolute project roots.
- The compiler-semantics ID moves from
  `fa171c7a2d78cf17e6cb49bbec5c1eed8bee20033472b1953211104068589ba7` to
  `95deb33a8d416d7bf60f02a36e251a71c3ee6f046b7e475d7bae2fc5ddc3767d`:
  the accepted language changed, so §30.1 requires a new ID. Every committed
  lock and verification record is regenerated against it.
- Language `1.1` has its independent compiler-semantics ID
  `0accaf7b80d572e21451d5fa650d92a1a28dae799823931b2f756e448fe89996`;
  language-1.0 locks and generated artifacts remain byte-identical.
- The four 0.1.0 examples still format byte-identically and generate
  byte-identical Lean and LaTeX modules; their source maps and manifests
  differ only in the source and semantic digests those artifacts embed. No
  previously-accepted run changed its generated bytes (§30.2).

### Not claimed

- This is not a §30 release. `cargo xtask release-check` refuses at `0.1.1`,
  and the release criterion is met only at `1.0.0`.
- The native Atlas graph's verification status is a `build` claim: it elaborates,
  replays, and reports no axiom outside Lean's own. The mathematical content
  is the specification's, cited at `some-true`, and the Lean kernel and
  elaborator beneath it are cited, not verified; the honest claim is that the
  Atlas is as sound as Lean 4.32.1, not that it is sound absolutely.
- Verified status is claimed by `verify` alone. `check` and `build` never
  claim it (`VR-18`), and `leanchecker` is a same-kernel replay, never
  described as an independent checker (§22.4).

## 0.1.0

The initial implementation of `LEXLEAN-SPEC-1`.

### Implemented

All 216 conformance IDs of SPEC.md §31 are implemented at honesty level
`build`: constructed in this repository and validated against an oracle by the
test named `conformance_<id>`. [CONFORMANCE.md](CONFORMANCE.md) is the
generated register, [ERRORS.md](ERRORS.md) the closed diagnostic registry, and
[VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md) the falsifiability record for every gate.

- Closed project configuration, canonical lock file, and offline dependency
  policy (`CF-01`..`CF-16`).
- Total lexical closure over every accepted atom (`LX-01`..`LX-14`) and
  versioned lexicon packages with closed schemas, denotations, and renderer
  tokens (`GL-01`..`GL-16`).
- The fixed structural, mathematical, and proposition grammar with closed
  ambiguity handling (`GR-01`..`GR-16`), the typed closed IR with canonical
  serialization, native modules, and language-1.1 snapshots (`SM-01`..`SM-16`),
  and generic semantic declarations plus document definitions with exact
  self-application and acyclicity rules (`DF-01`..`DF-11`).
- The structured proof language with pinned Lean lowerings (`PF-01`..`PF-18`),
  prose-free deterministic generated Lean with complete token traceability
  (`LN-01`..`LN-12`), and canonical LaTeX regeneration with the optional
  hash-checked PDF provider (`TX-01`..`TX-12`).
- Canonical diagnostics, source maps, coverage, manifests, and reproducible
  builds (`AR-01`..`AR-14`); fifteen-stage verification with `leanchecker`
  replay and exact axiom audit (`VR-01`..`VR-19`); the exact CLI contract and
  the stable seven-method Rust `Engine` API (`CL-01`..`CL-20`); filesystem
  confinement, no shell, no hidden network, and the closed failure model
  (`SE-01`..`SE-12`).
- Six example projects that verify under the pinned `leanprover/lean4:v4.32.1`
  toolchain, and the complete negative fixture suite (`EX-01`..`EX-08`).

### Not claimed

- This is not a §30 release. `cargo xtask release-check` refuses at `0.1.0`,
  and the release criterion is met only at `1.0.0`.
- Verified status is claimed by `verify` alone. `check` and `build` never claim
  it (`VR-18`), and `leanchecker` is a same-kernel replay, never described as
  an independent checker (§22.4).
- Facts about external tools are level `some-true` rows in
  [`model/ledger.toml`](model/ledger.toml): reproduced from cited authorities,
  not established here.
- The normative verification and reproducibility gate runs on Linux x86-64
  (§8.3). The other four supported hosts build the crate and run every test
  that does not need the pinned toolchain or a POSIX shell; each such case
  reports which assertions it did not run.

### Known deviations

The README's "Documented deviations" section lists every place the generated
bytes differ from a literal reading of SPEC.md, with the reason. Each is
enforced by the same golden and conformance gates as everything else.

# Changelog

## [0.1.0](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/compare/v0.1.0-rc.1...v0.1.0) (2026-11-11)


### Features Added

* **deploy:** each service is an image of its own, run apart and exercised (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([#81](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/81)) ([991ab33](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/991ab332608727306977c9850da6be182ab80071))
* **deploy:** mcp-loopback as a PrismPM host-effect system model (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([3124385](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/3124385b376642c58b29dd4fc74dcf323221c431))
* **deploy:** readiness commands and the key variable of the projection (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([2d619b8](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/2d619b8ed94279a3a365fc122cf41a7de7a8b6ac))
* **engine-host:** the four Engine calls are made by a program of their own (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([#74](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/74)) ([3053052](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/305305266658932dee42aceef6abf85df08f84b4))
* **model:** prismpm check passes on the model and runs in just vv (Part of [#5](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/5), [#14](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/14), [#15](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/15), [#18](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/18)) ([#79](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/79)) ([d5d6bfe](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/d5d6bfe27feb2e62546fe7ef932c298a99058294))
* **quality:** VP-07 executes the verify fixtures of Q1, and its clause narrows to the examples (Part of [#15](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/15)) ([#76](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/76)) ([20d7eaf](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/20d7eafbc37202ec10032ebbcec63f0bb57e9e63))
* **signer:** the signing key is held by a program of its own (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([#73](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/73)) ([0a54c34](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/0a54c34249b978a1cdab5288668a26d7c17e951f))
* **telemetry:** end each served request's span from the host's per-request methods (OB-15, Part of [#16](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/16)) ([0a7dbf9](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/0a7dbf9ff26690971890f13068163ef3e366d16f))
* **telemetry:** gap fingerprints, codes on S1 and S4, and a demand report (OB-16 to OB-18) ([6f70c19](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/6f70c1924fb780c123521e5c170df517a63bdea5))
* **telemetry:** record prism-code's gap fingerprints, codes on S1 and S4, and a demand report (OB-16 to OB-18, Part of [#16](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/16)) ([885b109](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/885b10941165aa37d70eb5da8e07f75177918a7a))
* **verifier:** every example but the Atlas verifies beside the CLI (Part of [#15](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/15)) ([#78](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/78)) ([c2715d2](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/c2715d284da08346b2ef7f9d2105563ff952c394))
* **verifier:** the process of each task is started by a program of its own (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([#80](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/80)) ([9a46f41](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/9a46f4139fba2e86cebf6f54814f819468460e96))


### Bugs Fixed

* **deploy:** the model builder is not a PrismPM release root ([b4b2d86](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/b4b2d86ca5777ed13614f63079fcb6e80ad44876))
* **drafts:** a draft that names no files selects its own files, not the profile's entrypoints ([#88](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/88)) ([f6128f2](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/f6128f227b271d07828ed319b118baf8c8580c05))
* **drafts:** a file of a draft replaces the profile's file at its path (Fixes [#84](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/84)) ([#85](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/85)) ([6abea22](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/6abea22c506c7f454fa2380b520052e80ab0bcda))
* **nfc-oracle:** re-export the packages for the project with Deployment ([f1fdf8a](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/f1fdf8ae6ca9bb54bea9be54ff31cce73a9bca37))
* **telemetry:** read an event stream's last answer from the end (clippy double_ended_iterator_last) ([6466b4c](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/6466b4c33eaf2bfa4c085a5858b14d7e1d634c2a))
* **telemetry:** rfind the last answer of an event stream (clippy filter_next) ([e61b8e7](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/e61b8e7b9bf6cb9a60c1dafd151c90e0761adb2b))


### Other Changes

* **deploy:** a release root waits on the server application of PrismPM[#342](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/342) (Part of [#17](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/issues/17)) ([889c0b5](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/lexlean-mcp/commit/889c0b56a7a45ad2e0f632cca2d0b509b7f56835))

changelog.text:
# Changelog

Every release of the `prismpm` crate and the SDK has an entry here, newest first.
The `prism-code` npm package has its own: [sdk/npm/prism-code/CHANGELOG.md](sdk/npm/prism-code/CHANGELOG.md).

Each entry uses the four headers [STABILITY.md](STABILITY.md) section 2 sets, in this order: Features Added, Breaking Changes, Bugs Fixed, Other Changes.
Breaking Changes is the per-version breaking log.
Before 1.0 a minor bump may break you and a patch bump never does; from 1.0 on, versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
The 0.1.0 entry predates this rule and keeps its original headers.

To move to 1.0, read the [migration guide](docs/site/migration/to-1-0.md).

## Policy

### Compatibility
- Holo/1 and accepted Prism application inputs remain stable. Additive contracts use new registered schemas; an incompatible schema change requires a new schema identifier and an explicit migration.

## [0.5.0](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0) (2026-11-14)

### Features Added

* **factory:** release cut by the certified plan; one workspace version for the release line ([96aa797](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/96aa797d1abd88dae2fa9907f452d14cf240d38e))
* **factory:** route release obligations through the certified Prism factory (port of [#586](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/586)) ([6dcdfb4](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/6dcdfb41e2407aa14d0672d51d1f5ad402e2c0e9))
* **factory:** the LexLean pin test is release plumbing ([bb4b725](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/bb4b725dec2ad60b4dbe580d8fd9f981c88c6912))
* **holo:** holo v5 is a UORC archive named by κ (ADR-017) ([#663](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/663)) ([7b48b4d](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/7b48b4d4939a7fa42c623c4a596357384fbe1566))
* **journey:** prism_build names the running stage ([#598](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/598)) ([82162af](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/82162af8227ab76073d971fa84ce646927f55de3))
* **prism-code:** a draft form of prism/spec/1, so a model only translates ([#667](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/667)) ([cdced92](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/cdced9240fd8456c215d56bb4982fa38136a8ad5))
* **prism-code:** axioms only from Lean's three, local-only setup, init relock, reproducible statement time ([#649](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/649)) ([94cb33c](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/94cb33c96bb59ce2229a0a32acf5f26bacad084b))
* **prism-code:** canonical path, integrity fails every policy, refuse text, local by default ([#648](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/648)) ([6b2c684](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/6b2c6844e3df025ca6ddb25a4052695dcc75805d))
* **prism-code:** check the developer surface against the developer view's glossary ([#347](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/347)) ([#614](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/614)) ([43127f8](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/43127f8091a4bc14f55b92d5f41da6c7c62f7d4c))
* **prism-code:** CLI groups named after the modules (Part of [#441](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/441)) ([#625](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/625)) ([b39812a](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/b39812a7204e71e436086e7f0bc35b72926c04ee))
* **prism-code:** Docker's spellings and the familiarity transcript (Part of [#347](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/347)) ([#637](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/637)) ([3263e7d](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/3263e7db15431acf56e73f38489366c296f72e9a))
* **prism-code:** finish prism.containers and prism.volumes, SDK and CLI (Part of [#443](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/443)) ([#620](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/620)) ([287040c](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/287040c65372ab94ebba9f579e524abb5c87b978))
* **prism-code:** generate --lang rust and --lang python ([#589](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/589)) ([0df1b03](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/0df1b03dd60eddfeceebc975f305dc68dc8e2bb6))
* **prism-code:** local image store, prism.images list/tag/remove/prune and prism-code images (Closes [#349](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/349), Part of [#442](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/442)) ([#622](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/issues/622)) ([a6c17d0](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/prismpm/commit/a6c17d06b86518b4dc30028a7bdff27f3cfb0096))
